extracted.intended_audience: eRA Commons users: PIs, Signing Officials (SOs), Account Administrators, Sponsors, Trainees, and NIH/Agency internal users
extracted.subtask_short: eRA Commons account setup and roles
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for registering institutions, creating and managing eRA Commons accounts, role privileges (PI, SO, Sponsor, Trainee), login methods, password policy, and admin/module operations for using the eRA Commons system. Covers procedural steps and system constraints for external and internal users.

rubrics_metrics.name: e-PI model intent
rubrics_metrics.description: e-PI model is intended to supplement—not replace—the traditional single-PI model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States the policy context for applying multi-PI functionality (i.e., e-PI supplements single-PI model).

rubrics_metrics.name: PI privileges and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If you hold a PI role, you have privileges to perform the following tasks: Edit your personal profile (PPF); Delegate edit authority of your own PPF to others; View the status of all grant applications for which you are the designated PI, including any errors or warnings; View the assembled image of submitted grant applications before those grants move on for further processing; View Study Section/Meeting Roster of the Review Group that will be reviewing your application; View Review outcome information and summary statements; View Notice of Award (NoA) for all grants for which you are the designated PI; Delegate authority to someone with an ASST role to perform the same actions and receive the same notifications as you do as the PI; View Training Grant related items using xTrain (Trainee Roster, List of Grants, Grant Summary, Routing History, PDF-formatted Appointments/Amendments/Terminations); Initiate, update, route, and submit Appointments, Re-Appointments, and Amendments in xTrain; Initiate, update, and route Termination Notices in xTrain; Initiate a progress report; Delegate progress report authority; Submit a progress report when given the authority by an SO; Delegate Status authority to others within the institution so that they can see PI grant information (except Review outcome information and Summary Statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOTES: PI users cannot delegate authority to submit appointments to the Agency. The PI role should not be combined with the SO role, but can be combined with the IAR role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing Official (SO) privileges and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: An SO has institutional authority to legally bind the institution in grant-administration matters by providing signature approval on grant application submissions. If you hold an SO role, you have privileges to perform the following tasks: Register the applicant institution in Commons; Create and update the Institutional Profile (IPF); Create/delete/update all Commons accounts (except IAR and TRAINEE accounts); Create affiliation between an existing PD/PI and/or IAR Commons account and the institution; Submit electronic grant application(s) on behalf of the institution via Grants.gov (outside of eRA Commons), if also registered with Grants.gov as the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR); View status of all grant applications originating from their institution and any errors or warnings; View assembled image of submitted grant applications before they move on for further processing; Reject grant applications to address submission warnings; View award information for all grants awarded to the institution; Submit JIT information for a PD/PI; View xTrain items (Trainee Roster, List of Grants, Grant Summary, Routing History, PDF-formatted Appointments/Amendments/Terminations); Delegate progress report authority to someone on behalf of the PD/PI; Delegate submit authority for progress reports to a PD/PI; Submit a progress report to the Agency (NIH); Submit Final Progress Reports (FPRs); Submit a one-time No-Cost Extension on behalf of the PD/PI; Assign the FCOI role for those using the Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI) module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOTES: An SO cannot modify another user's personal profile (PPF) unless designated to do so by that user. An SO cannot view summary statements or priority scores. NOTE: An SO role should never be combined with a PI role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor role privileges (xTrain)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sponsor supervises the research training experience of individual fellows supported by fellowship awards in the xTrain module. If you hold a Sponsor role, you have privileges to: View Training Grant related items (Trainee Roster, List of Grants); Review Termination Notices and route to BO before submission to Agency; Initiate Termination Notices on behalf of fellows who have left the institution; Delegate Sponsor authority to another individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor role is associated with all fellowships for which you are a Sponsor and can be added by institutional SO or other account managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee role privileges (xTrain)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commons xTrain TRAINEE role is used to manage electronic appointments for awarded Training Grants. If you hold a TRAINEE role, you have privileges to: View your PDF-formatted Appointments/Amendments/Terminations; Update and route your Appointments/Amendments/Terminations; View Appointments/Amendments/Terminations routing history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trainee role is scoped to the trainee's appointment records in xTrain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commons login authentication (Commons User ID)
rubrics_metrics.description: To log into Commons with a Commons User ID: Navigate to the Commons system, enter your username (6 to 20 characters) and password, and click Login. Passwords display as asterisks; the Commons system will lock users out after three (3) unsuccessful login attempts (note: other sections list different lock thresholds). A successful login shows the username, institution, and your user roles in the Welcome section and the upper right corner of every Commons screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMPORTANT: If affiliated with multiple institutions, verify the correct institution is displayed after login as it affects accessible information. The modules accessible depend on the user’s role and privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network ID (NIH/Agency) login
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal NIH or Agency users access Commons using their Network ID (the same ID used to sign onto their computer). From the Network ID login page, insert your PIV card into the card reader OR enter your Network User Name and Password and press Log in. Do not enter your IMPAC II credentials. If first time, you may be directed to synchronize your network account with your IMPAC II account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of federal users who may need Commons access include OFM staff, administrators managing xTRAIN appointments, and Scientific Review Officers (SROs). All Commons users — including federal staff — must have a Commons role to log in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Session expiration policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Work sessions expire after 45 minutes of inactivity, at which time the system returns to the Commons Login screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If going to be away for an extended period, save changes and log out to avoid losing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federated Institutions/Organizations Sign In (pilot)
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA Commons pilots Institution/Organization Log In functionality allowing users at registered institutions (with CIT) to use their organization's credentials to log into Commons and link to their Commons account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If credentials are not linked, users are prompted to link by entering Commons User ID and password. Validations occur with the organization; failures must be addressed with the organization. During the pilot, some Commons features may be limited for federated users; if difficulties occur, log in using your eRA User ID and password.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federated account linking constraints and troubleshooting
rubrics_metrics.description: Common reasons linking may fail: using a temporary password (must change to a permanent one before linking); Commons password expired (must change); account locked due to multiple unsuccessful logins (reset via Forgot Password/Unlock Account link).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of these apply, contact the eRA Helpdesk. Carefully read screen messages and tips during the linking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining a single Commons account when switching institutions (PIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs moving institutions should maintain a single Commons account and affiliate the new institution to that account rather than creating a new account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits: cohesive grant history, reviewer service recorded, accurate NIH records, degree information maintained for Early Stage Investigator eligibility. Steps: request SO at new institution to affiliate your existing Commons account (provide Commons ID); if you left the old institution, request the old SO to disaffiliate you; contact eRA Help Desk if you have more than one Commons account to merge. IMPORTANT: While a PI can keep the same account, SOs must create a new account within the new institution/organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing displayed affiliated institution
rubrics_metrics.description: If affiliated with multiple institutions, the selected institution (displayed as a link in the upper right) determines which institution's information you can access. To change: log in, click the institution link, select the radio button for desired institution, click Submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grant and institution information displayed is only for the selected institution. This change can be made from any screen in Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password creation standards (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for creating passwords: Must be at least eight (8) characters long (no blank spaces) and is case sensitive; Must contain a combination of at least three (3) of the following types of characters: Uppercase letters, Lowercase letters, Numeric characters, Special characters (! # $ % - _ = + < > *).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The following special characters are NOT allowed: @, &, or a 'period'. Passwords may NOT contain your Username and may NOT start or end with a number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password lifecycle and reuse rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Passwords cannot be reused within one year and must be changed every 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passwords created or changed by the Institute and/or Center (IC) Account Administrators must be changed at first login.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account lockout and temporary password rules (multiple statements present)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts may be locked after multiple unsuccessful login attempts: one section states lock after three (3) unsuccessful login attempts; another states accounts are locked after six (6) consecutive unsuccessful login attempts. Users can click the Forgot Password/Unlock Account? link to unlock; a temporary password will be forwarded to the account owner's email and is active for only 48 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If still experiencing issues, users can contact the eRA/Commons help desk (866-504-9552/commons@od.nih.gov). NOTE: Temporary passwords sent via email are only valid for 48 hours and must be changed to a permanent password within that time period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reset Password procedure (forgot password)
rubrics_metrics.description: To reset a forgotten password: select the Forgot Password/Unlock Account? link on the Commons home page, enter your User ID and Email address on the Reset Password screen, and click Submit. Commons generates a new temporary password and sends it to the email in the user profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must be able to access that email account to receive the temporary password. After logging in with the temporary password, create and enter a new password as prompted. All passwords are validated against the Password Policy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing password while logged in
rubrics_metrics.description: When logged in, change your account password using Admin > Accounts > Change Password. Enter current password, enter new password and confirm, then Submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Change Password screen lists the password creation standards. Password changes take effect immediately and must be used on next login.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resetting an expired password
rubrics_metrics.description: When your password has expired, you are directed to select a new password when you try to log in. Enter Current Password, Enter a New Password, Re-enter the new password in Confirm, and Submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new password must conform to the standards listed on the screen and is effective immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resetting a locked account (SO involvement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an account is locked due to multiple invalid login attempts, the Signing Official (SO) at your organization must unlock the account and reset the password. SOs can reset locked accounts with the Manage Accounts feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Accounts Management module has online help for unlocking and resetting locked accounts. If your account is not locked but you've forgotten your password, you can reset it yourself via the Forgot Password flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logging out best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of any work, edits, updates, submissions or administrative changes, log off/sign out from the Commons system before closing the browser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Logout link is located in the upper right corner of each screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modules and role-dependent access
rubrics_metrics.description: Commons is organized by modules; your access to each module and its features depends on your assigned user role(s). The Admin module houses features used to perform Account Management and Delegations. If you have access, a module is visible on the navigation menu bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOTE: The UI images are for display only and the available modules depend on the displayed role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admin module - Accounts functions
rubrics_metrics.description: From Account Administration you can Manage Accounts, perform Advanced Search, and Change Password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To access Accounts: select Admin tab, then Accounts tab. Refer to Accounts Module Online Help or Accounts Management User Guide for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Search (Accounts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrators (e.g., SO) can perform an advanced search on existing Commons accounts to locate PIs eligible for continuous submission. The percent sign (%) may be used as a wildcard (e.g., Sm%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced Search allows searching accounts within your institution or including those outside your institution (scope determined by role/permissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commons Demonstration Site usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commons Demonstration Site is a fully functioning training environment with sample data for users to practice account creation and grant application tasks. Creation of an SO and a PI account is required, with sample grant applications assigned to the created institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Demo Facility link from the login page. Demo account usernames must be unique; username must be 6-20 characters. All fields followed by an asterisk (*) are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registering institutions - prerequisite and process
rubrics_metrics.description: To register an extramural institution you must have a valid and verifiable Dunn and Bradstreet (DUNS) number before proceeding. The initial registration creates a mandatory SO account and an optional AA account. Only authorized organization officials may be deemed SOs (examples: Corporation President/CEO; Institute Executive Director; University President/Dean/Chancellor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access the Online Registration system via Register Grantee Organization link. Complete institution and account information, verify entered information, print and sign the registration form (ONLY the SO may sign), fax the signed form to NIH (301-451-5675), and click the email hyperlink sent to the SO to verify the SO's email address. The signed form must be faxed and the email verified before registration begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution registration confirmation and email flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the SO's email is confirmed and NIH reviews the registration, NIH sends a second email with status (approved/rejected) and, if approved, a hyperlink to finalize registration. Upon finalizing, emails are sent with the Commons user name in one and a temporary password in another for the SO (and separately for AA if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After logging into Commons with the temporary password, the user is prompted to change the password per NIH password policy. AA receives separate emails; SO emails do not include AA credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration form and field constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration form constraints: All fields followed by a red asterisk (*) are required; a minimum of one address line (Street 1) is required; Institution Name may contain up to 100 characters; an Official’s Title may contain up to 240 characters; User Name must be 6 to 20 characters (numbers and letters combined, no spaces); account names must be unique; DUNS Number is a unique nine-digit identification for single business entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AA position information is optional; when creating an AA provide required fields. More information about DUNS Numbers is online at http://www.dnb.com/us/.
